comments.body: Also: carrot's declared wait survived a compaction (muster pane compact) - after it, the pane showed 0% context and still 'waiting ... on melon re-checking two review fixes', so muster pane wait --until idle timed out at 300 s on an idle agent.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body:
2026-11-01 re-triage: two more rounds hit this, from tooling feedback. In a parallel-work round in another project, three Claude Code workers posted 'slot N done' and ended their turns at an empty prompt, yet `muster window` kept each `waiting` on its old declared reason ('on review from laurel', 'on re-review from engine', 'on Codex review of FFI commits') for 34 s to 6 min after the report. In Foreman's round the same day, worker teal stayed `waiting` for 12+ minutes after posting 'slot 1 done' and through a `muster pane compact`, so `pane wait --until idle --timeout 300` timed out twice and stalled the integrator's compact-then-brief sequence.

This follows the documented rule (`docs/cli/agents.md`, under `pane wait`): a declared wait outlasts a turn Muster typed, such as a message wake, and then lasts up to 10 minutes. A worker waiting on its reviewer is woken by exactly such a turn, the review arriving, so the wait outlives the work it was for. The feedback suggests clearing the wait on Stop, but that would break every wait, since an agent declares one at the end of the turn it then stops. The fix has to tell a wake that delivers what the agent was waiting for from one that does not, or end a carried wait once the agent posts and ends its turn. teal's 12+ minutes is past the 10-minute cap: check whether teal declared again or the cap missed it. Moved to backlog-hi: integrators sequence on `--until idle`, and this times them out.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-03: ending a carried wait once the agent posts and ends its turn would bring back the bug d590527b fixed. There a helper waiting on its own build was woken by an unrelated message from its maker, answered, and did not declare again, so it read idle with the build running and its maker was told it had gone idle without reporting. Answering is a post, so that rule clears the wait in exactly that case. The two cases differ in who sent the waking message: here it came from the thing waited on (the reviewer), there from someone else. Candidate fix: let a wait name the agent it waits on, `report --waiting "<what>" --until-message-from <pane>`, beside --until-exits; a message from that pane ends it and any other wake carries it as today. Awaiting the owner's go-ahead.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: Done 2026-11-05: 5c6a67d4..630b9297 on main. report --waiting --until-message-from <pane> ends on a wake from that pane; teal's overrun explained: each carry restarts a carried wait's 10-minute timer (wait serial), and takeover restarts it too. The tai parallel-work skill gets the flag once the installed Muster has it.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-28 in a parallel-work round, twice: anvil and carrot (Claude Code workers, helpers of tulip) each declared a wait on their own reviewers with report --waiting, got the reviews back, finished, posted 'slot N done' to the integrator and ended their turns at an empty prompt. muster window then showed each as 'waiting ... on review from elder' / 'on melon re-checking two review fixes' rather than done or idle. Impact: the integrator reads a finished worker as still busy. Check whether a turn that ends after a post should clear a declared wait, or whether the agent re-declared it at the end of its last turn (pane read --turn did not show it).


Decided 2026-11-03 (amterp): a declared wait can name the agent it waits on, `report --waiting "<what>" --until-message-from <pane>`, beside `--until-exits <pid>`. A message wake from that pane ends the wait; a wake for anyone else's message carries it as today. A wait declared without the flag keeps today's behavior, so d590527b's fix stands: there a helper waiting on its build answered its maker's unrelated message and read idle with the build still running. Ending a carried wait on any post, the other option considered, would bring that back, since answering is a post. Done also means the parallel-work skill (tai) and `extras/skill/SKILL.md` tell an agent waiting on a reviewer or helper to use the flag, `docs/cli/agents.md` and `docs/architecture.md` describe it, and teal's 12+ minutes past the 10-minute cap is explained.
title: A worker that posted its report and ended its turn still reads waiting on a wait it declared earlier
